INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
FISERV
Azeez Dandawala, CS B. Tech 2019-23
Round 1: Group Discussion (25 mins)
6 people were present in each group and 2 topics were given to every group out of which
we had to select one.
We were given a choice between Women Empowerment & Gender justice and Merits &
Demerits of a cashless economy, out of which we chose the former one.
Each one of us had to share our opinions and views on the topic. We discussed the
problems that women are facing, solutions/ideas to overcome those problems,
achievements made so far by women, steps taken by the government on women
empowerment in rural areas, etc.
Some tips to win the group discussion:
●
Clarify the topic beforehand with the panel.
●
Make sure the points that you present are clear, concise, and relevant to the topic.
●
Carry a pen and notebook to jot down important points.
●
Listen more than you speak :)
●
Be positive during the group discussion.
44 people were shortlisted for the technical round.
1

Round 2: Technical Round (20 mins)
I was asked to introduce myself (mug it up xD!)
The interviewer continued by asking me my language of choice to which I replied C++.
He then asked me to explain OOPS, Polymorphism, Data Abstraction, and the real-world
significance of these terminologies. Try explaining the concepts with the help of examples.
I was asked a question about abstract classes in Java(I had mentioned Java in my resume). I
explained abstract classes, pure abstraction using interfaces, etc.
Next, questions on DBMS were asked like what are clauses in SQL?, What is DDL? And What
is a software development lifecycle? (I was not so familiar with this question).
Finally, I was asked if I had any questions for them (Always ask a question).
32 people were shortlisted for the managerial round.
Round 3: Managerial Round (15 mins)
Introduce yourself (again, mug it up!)
This was sort of an HR round, the interviewer asked me to explain any one of my projects.
Make sure you have a clear understanding of your project and the ability to explain it in
simple terms. Further, I was asked about my interests apart from coding.
Lastly, I was asked to share my view on the impact of electric cars on India. (Always look for
some unique points, in my case, I talked about the effect on the economy i.e.  benefits to
the state by reducing fuel costs and shifting consumption away from imported oil to more
locally produced electricity sources.)
21 students were shortlisted for the internship and I was lucky to be one of them :)
2
